comments.text:
Indonesia’s territory excluding the EEZ consists of approximately:

* Land area: ~1.9 million km²
* Internal, archipelagic and territorial waters: ~3.1 million km²
* Total land + sovereign waters: approximately 5.0 million km²

This does not include Indonesia’s EEZ, which extends up to 200 nautical miles and covers roughly 6.16 million km².

In short: Indonesia’s land and sovereign waters together cover about 5 million km², excluding the EEZ.

comments.author: @Jhonhero007
comments.text:
Base on Internasional law, that indonesia is Maritime country, it means not only land but also own sea area, Indonesia’s total territory can be broadly divided into land and water:

* 🟩 Land area: approximately 1.9 million km²
* 🟦 Marine/water area: approximately 3.3 million km²
* 🌏 Total territory: approximately 5.2 million km²

This means Indonesia’s marine area is about 1.7 times larger than its land area.

Approximate composition

* Land: ~36%
* Sea/water: ~64%

Indonesia is therefore a maritime and archipelagic country. Although its land area is smaller than India’s, its enormous maritime territory makes its overall geographical area very large.

The exact figures vary depending on the definition used—for example, whether the calculation includes only territorial waters or also Indonesia’s Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ).
